text:
Tim Washe is an undrafted center from Detroit by way of Western Michigan, and he's carved out a real role in Anaheim: 15 minutes a night, three goals and six points in 20 games, already more than last season's five points in 39. He hits (57) and blocks shots (29), and he kills penalties.

The last few weeks have been quiet. He's gone nine games without a point, and the reason is mostly the team around him: the Ducks have scored 6.7 fewer goals than their chances with him on. His own shooting is fine, a bit high at 15%.

The harder truth is the shot share. Anaheim gets only 40% of the five-on-five expected goals with him on, almost seven points worse than without him, and Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking said last season that his game isn't built on creating offense. He plays like Ben Meyers and Morgan Barron: checking-line centers whose value is in the defensive details. On a young, winning Ducks team, that's a job. Whether it's a 15-minute job is the question we'd keep an eye on.
